entries.title: Spider-Verse — Script to Film Study
entries.content:
SOURCE
Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse screenplay, compared with the corresponding film sequence.

SEQUENCE
At Visions Academy, Miles deliberately tries to score zero because he wants to leave. His teacher sees that he knows the answer, changes the score to 100, and makes clear that his wish to return to Brooklyn will not decide the matter. Miles feels socially misplaced at the school, then turns to Aaron for relief. Their trip through the tunnels leads to the graffiti wall: Aaron crosses the electrified gate with ease; Miles struggles, accepts some help, and completes the work. While the moment feels freeing, the spider moves closer and bites him.

SCRIPT → FILM
The screenplay gives the essential skeleton of the actions and turns. The film builds the exact choreography, visual detail, montage rhythm, rap-like music, and fast cutting around it. Some film actions are not written, and some written blocking changes—for example, the film does not simply hold on Aaron while Miles climbs the gate—but the dramatic structure remains. Pre-lap audio and occasional dual dialogue were also noticeable.

EMOTIONAL MOVEMENT
Quiet alienation and frustration shift into affection, recognition, and creative fulfilment with Aaron. The spider keeps a thread of curiosity and future unease alive beneath the release.

TRANSFERABLE TECHNIQUE
Describe the essential structure of physical action. Specify movements that carry story, character, emotion, or timing; let direction, performance, editing, sound, and animation determine the full execution.

entries.title: Observation 03 — Knowing, but Still Asking
entries.content:
During class, groups of students were called outside and returned smiling after learning they had been placed in Model A. When my own friend group returned, everyone except Manish and me had been selected. I stayed quiet and continued listening to the teacher. Manish kept asking classmates whether his name was on the list, even after being told it was not. He asked to change seats so he could speak to one selected friend. He repeatedly said, “I know,” but continued searching.

POSSIBLE MOTIVE
He may have been hoping the answer would somehow change, or needed reassurance before accepting it.

entries.title: Observation 04 — The Assumed Transfer
entries.content:
An opening appeared in our section when one student moved to Model A. A student from Model A asked to take the place. The vice-principal later said he had moved to be with a friend, and the class laughed because Model A was considered more desirable. After learning our section was Model B, he asked whether the student who had replaced him would swap back. The vice-principal referred to the written transfer requests and scolded him for creating the confusion.

POSSIBLE MOTIVE
He may have acted on an assumption about the section instead of choosing it for friendship.

entries.title: MODEL B — Scene 1
entries.content:
DRAFT RECORD
Draft 1: first one-page scene based on Observation 03.
Draft 2: intermediate revision.
Draft 3: corrected Day 2 version.

SCENE FOCUS
Manish wants confirmation that he belongs in Model A. His repeated questions and searching actions show his resistance to accepting the result.

DAY 2 REVISION
The opening now shows the classroom interruption and the batches returning rather than only summarising it. The final exchange clarifies the outcome. All three versions are preserved above.

entries.title: Hangul Recall, Decoding & Dictation
entries.content:
LESSON
Hangul recall, vowel contrasts, shuffled block decoding, and selection dictation.

RECALL
Twenty known letters and blocks were read aloud in chat. Main corrected labels: ㅓ = eo, ㅡ = eu; 내 = nae; 네 = ne; 게 = ge; 무 = mu.

SHUFFLED DECODING
First attempt: 14/20.
Corrected and retested: 내 = nae, 느 = neu, 네 = ne, 그 = geu, 게 = ge, 무 = mu.
Retest: 5/6, then 내 = nae corrected.

SELECTION DICTATION
Ten-item multiple-choice block dictation, used because there was no paper and the keyboard was in Korean.
Score: 8/10.
Corrected pairs: 너 = neo / 느 = neu; 루 = ru / 로 = ro.

STARRED CONTRASTS FOR RETEST
ㅓ vs ㅡ; 너 vs 느; 루 vs 로; ㅐ vs ㅔ.

PRONUNCIATION
Not assessed today. This result measures reading and recognition, not spoken accuracy.

entries.title: Spider-Verse — Power Becomes Public
entries.content:
SOURCE
Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse screenplay, pages 19–29 approximately, compared with the corresponding film sequence.

ANALYSIS
After the spider bite, Miles wants to remain normal, unnoticed and in control. Instead, his body changes overnight: he grows, his clothes no longer fit, and he feels exposed at Visions Academy. His powers turn that private panic into public embarrassment when his hand sticks to Gwen's hair. He then flees security, discovers that he can cling to walls, and creates more chaos while trying to escape. Back at the tunnel, he crosses the electrified gate that he could not cross before, showing that the change is real and growing. The dead spider glitches when he touches it, creating a concrete sense that something is unstable; this is useful foreshadowing, but it does not by itself prove when later films were planned. Miles follows his spider-sense into the collider fight, where Peter Parker saves him and tells him he has no choice about being involved. By the end, Miles can no longer treat his abilities as a private accident with no wider consequence.

SCRIPT → FILM
The film follows the screenplay's main action and turns closely, while adding comic-style thought bubbles, reaction shots, fast cutting, sound and more precise physical comedy.

TRANSFERABLE TECHNIQUE
Show inner panic through a chain of physical problems and escalating public consequences. A graphic device such as thought bubbles works only when the film's visual style supports it; in a conventional screenplay, write the observable behavior instead of naming the emotion.

entries.title: Observation 05 — Chosen Proximity
entries.content:
During Monday CSDQ exam sessions, Student B repeatedly chose a seat in the row parallel to Student A. During 15-minute breaks, she carried her chair to the end of the girls’ row nearest his place at the edge of the boys’ row. She sometimes looked toward him and they briefly spoke. Student A kept working and did not extend the interaction.

POSSIBLE MOTIVE
She may be seeking proximity, while he may be trying to keep distance. The stated history between them is not treated as camera-verifiable evidence.

entries.title: Observation 06 — The Consolation That Fails
entries.content:
After losing his badminton matches, a player sat at the side of the court while other matches continued. He asked others if he could play, then began jogging laps around the court. A coach stopped him and asked whether he knew he had been eliminated. Nearby, another player who had lost sat silently while the coach spoke to her. The coach praised the runner’s smile and told him to encourage her. He said, “Take it easy.” She stared; he resumed jogging.

TRANSFERABLE SCENE ENGINE
Visible goal: remain involved and composed. Resistance: elimination and the coach’s public instruction. Turn: the attempted consolation fails, so he retreats into motion.

entries.title: MODEL B — Scene 1 · Drafts 4–5
entries.content:
DRAFT 4
The scene continues after Manish learns about Model A. He wants to check whether his name is on the list and tries to switch places to speak to Aditya. Nitish blocks the attempt and Manish returns to his notebook while still watching the selected students.

DRAFT 5 QUALITY PASS
The resistance is made concrete: Nitish says the selection is the final call. The intentional dual dialogue remains, including Manish cutting in to complete “final call,” which expresses his urgency.

SCENE CHECK
Goal: learn whether he can be in Model A. Resistance: the decision is final and he cannot leave his place to get confirmation. Changed tactic: he first presses to speak to Aditya, then softens the request into wanting “information.” End state: he returns to work without resolution, leaving the earlier line unfinished.

entries.title: Plain vs Aspirated Consonants
entries.content:
CONTRASTS
Plain: ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ. Aspirated: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ. Tense forms (ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅉ) were identified as a separate future lesson.

RECALL
Known-block recall: 8/8.

MIXED IDENTIFICATION
Aspirated versus plain blocks: 20/20.

WORD READING
커피, 치마, 토마토, 파도, 코, 피, 차, 키, 포도, 타다. Result: 9/10. Correction: 키 = ki, not gi. 커피 was corrected as keo-pi.

CONTRAST PRACTICE
가/카, 다/타, 바/파, 자/차, 기/키 were produced aloud. The learner reported the stronger burst on the aspirated member; spoken accuracy was not independently assessed.

STAR FOR RETEST
키 versus 기; ㅓ in 커피.
